channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Pakistan's Counterterrorism Operations in Afghanistan Are Defensive, Envoy States
item.description: Pakistan's special representative for Afghanistan, Mohammad Sadiq, stated at the "Moscow Format" meeting that counterterrorism operations are defensive responses to attacks from Afghanistan. He cited intelligence-based, precise actions taken under self-defense rights, noting over 4,700 Pakistani citizens killed in such attacks over three years. Sadiq also highlighted the presence of TTP, BLA, ISKP, and al-Qaeda in Afghanistan.

item.title: Global Grain Prices May Rise 80% Due to Strait of Hormuz Disruptions, Experts Warn
item.description: Global food security could be threatened by disruptions to shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, potentially causing grain prices to increase by up to 80% in some regions, according to experts. Logistical bottlenecks have already reduced export volumes by 40%. The El Niño phenomenon is exacerbating the situation. Kazakhstan has set its 2026 grain purchase price and implemented measures to support farmers and stimulate exports.

item.title: UN Human Rights Council Extends Richard Bennett's Mission in Afghanistan for Another Year
item.description: The UN Human Rights Council has extended Richard Bennett's mandate as Special Rapporteur for Afghanistan for another year. The resolution requires Bennett to prepare a study on the situation of "minorities" in Afghanistan and present it in September 2027. It also includes an "enhanced interactive dialogue" on gender concerns in June 2027. Bennett's access to Afghanistan remains prohibited by the Taliban.

item.title: Uzbekistan Focuses on Environmental Sustainability and Green Economy Development
item.description: Uzbekistan is implementing systemic measures to protect the environment, rationally use natural resources, and develop a green economy as part of its National Sustainable Development Goals by 2030. Efforts include modernizing industrial facilities, improving water resource management, and expanding air and water quality monitoring systems. The nation has also planted millions of trees, increasing green spaces to 15 percent.

item.title: Kazakhstan Presents Experience in Developing Constitutional Justice in the Digital Age
item.description: Kazakhstan shared its experience in constitutional justice development during the digital era at the VII Congress of the Association of Asian Constitutional Courts and Equivalent Institutions (AACC) in Samarkand. The congress adopted the Samarkand Declaration, focusing on human rights protection, the rule of law, and international cooperation amidst digital transformation and AI advancements.

item.title: Astana Launches Application Process for 562 Credit-Funded Apartments
item.description: Astana has begun accepting applications for 562 credit-funded apartments available for eligible residents. The apartments, located in new buildings, are offered with finishing and feature a 5% interest rate. Interested individuals can submit applications through the Baspana Market online platform.

item.title: International Criminal Court Publicizes Arrest Warrants for Taliban Ministers
item.description: The International Criminal Court in The Hague has unsealed arrest warrants for four Taliban officials, including the group's leader. The warrants, issued in September 2025, target the ministers of education and higher education, along with Hibatullah Akhundzada and Abdul Hakim Haqqani. The court cited reasonable grounds to believe these individuals are responsible for crimes against humanity, specifically persecution based on gender and political affiliation.

item.title: Uzbekistan Representatives Participate in 153rd Inter-Parliamentary Union Assembly
item.description: Representatives from Uzbekistan are attending the 153rd Assembly of the Inter-Parliamentary Union (IPU) in Arusha, Tanzania. The delegation, led by Senate Chairperson Tanzila Narbaeva, is participating in discussions on effective governance, inclusivity, and equal opportunities. The assembly will also feature elections for a new IPU President and sessions on global issues like artificial intelligence and climate change.

item.title: UN: 5.8 Million Refugee Children to Miss School in 2025
item.description: The UN Refugee Agency (UNHCR) estimates that 5.8 million school-aged refugee children globally will not attend school in 2025, representing 44% of the total refugee child population. Reduced international funding threatens progress in educational access. A significant gap exists between primary and secondary education enrollment, with only 32% of refugees continuing to secondary school.

item.title: Kazakhstan Strengthens Asian Cooperation and Cultural Ties
item.description: Kazakhstan is expanding cooperation with foreign partners in investment, technology, business, and culture. A Kazakh musical film was screened at the ASEAN Film Festival in Hong Kong. Kazakhstan's Consulate General in Hong Kong discussed a forthcoming visit of Hong Kong manufacturers' association representatives to Kazakhstan. A new Honorary Consulate of Kazakhstan has opened in Daejeon, South Korea.

item.title: Uzbekistan Discovers Five New Gas Fields Since Start of Year, President's Office Reports
item.description: Uzbekistan has discovered five new natural gas fields since the beginning of the year, according to the presidential press service. Eighty wells have been drilled in various regions, some reaching depths over 6,000 meters. An additional 40 wells are planned for the fourth quarter.

item.title: Human Rights Watch: US Failed to Compensate Afghan War Crimes Victims After 25 Years
item.description: Human Rights Watch states that 25 years after the Afghanistan war began, the US and coalition partners have not provided justice or compensation for war crimes and human rights violations. The report details torture methods used by US forces and the lack of accountability for abuses.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Denmark Identify New Avenues for Cooperation
item.description: Uzbekistan's Foreign Minister Bakhtiyor Saidov met with Denmark's Foreign Minister Lars Løkke Rasmussen to discuss bilateral relations. Denmark is seen as a key European partner, with discussions focusing on political dialogue, green economy, scientific exchanges, and trade. A memorandum on political consultations was signed to institutionalize future discussions.

item.title: Police investigate school bomb threat report in Kostanay
item.description: Kostanay police have launched a pre-trial investigation following a bomb threat message targeting School No. 17, which circulated on Telegram. The school building was searched, and no explosives or suspicious items were found. Authorities are working to identify the sender of the message.

item.title: Extortion and shooting: Police open criminal case against head of public service center in Zhambyl region
item.description: Police in the Zhambyl region are investigating extortion allegations against the head of a public service center in Kyzylsharu village. The individual reportedly fired a shotgun near a resident's home after the resident requested money back. The Ministry of Internal Affairs confirmed a pre-trial investigation into extortion is underway.

item.title: Taliban Official in Herat Dismissed Over Allegations of Drug Sales at Treatment Center
item.description: Sources in Herat report that Hayatullah Rohani, head of the Taliban’s Counter-Narcotics Department, was dismissed following an investigation into allegations of selling drugs at an addiction treatment hospital. The investigation found that individuals under his command extorted patients for drugs. Despite evidence, Rohani has not been arrested.

item.title: Kazakhstan Railways Seeks 50% Increase in Passenger Locomotive Service Tariffs
item.description: Kazakhstan's passenger locomotive company has applied to the national regulator for a 50% increase in tariffs. The company cites rising costs for electricity, diesel fuel, crew services, and locomotive maintenance. The current prices have been in effect since 2018, and the anti-monopoly committee will review the request's economic justification.

item.title: Uzbek President Reviews Major Oil and Gas Projects, Emphasizes Efficiency
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev reviewed presentations of major oil and gas projects. He issued instructions to increase the efficiency of geological exploration and drilling operations. The president stressed the importance of conducting large-scale projects based on thorough calculations and clear financing sources.

item.title: Russian Governors Visit Fergana Region to Explore Investment and Industrial Potential
item.description: Governors from Russian regions are visiting Uzbekistan's Fergana region for the third meeting of the Council of Regions of Uzbekistan and the Russian Federation. The delegation is exploring major industrial enterprises, investment projects, and the region's production capabilities. They visited the "Crown Ceramic" joint venture, which plans significant annual production and exports.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev Welcomes Sultan of Oman at Astana Airport with Military Escort
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev received the Sultan of Oman, Haitham bin Tariq Al Said, upon his arrival in Astana for a state visit. Military aircraft escorted the Sultan's plane from the border. Tokayev highlighted the visit's historical significance for bilateral relations and expressed confidence in expanding cooperation.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Azerbaijan Celebrate 30 Years of Strategic Partnership and Cooperation
item.description: Uzbekistan and Azerbaijan mark 30 years of diplomatic relations, evolving from friendship to strategic partnership and alliance. The relationship now encompasses significant economic cooperation, investments, transport, energy projects, and humanitarian initiatives, building on a shared history and culture.

item.title: Uzbekistan Covers International Exam Costs for Over 74,000 Youth
item.description: Uzbekistan has reimbursed the costs of international exams for more than 74,000 young people, totaling 151 billion UZS. Specifically, over 54,000 individuals received 125 billion UZS in compensation for IELTS exams. This initiative supports youth participation in global educational opportunities.

item.title: Rubio Visits NATO Allies Amid Russian Concerns and Middle East Conflict
item.description: U.S. Secretary of State Antony Blinken is visiting Iceland, Greece, and Portugal from October 5-8 to discuss security, defense, energy, economic cooperation, and technology. The trip addresses growing concerns over Russian military activity and the Middle East conflict, with discussions focusing on Arctic security, regional stability, and defense partnerships.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev Discusses Partnership Potential with Sultan of Oman
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev held a brief meeting with the Sultan of Oman, Haitham bin Tarik Al Said, in Astana. Tokayev described the visit as historic, highlighting the significant potential for partnership between Kazakhstan and Oman, particularly in economic development and international mediation. Both leaders expressed confidence in fruitful future negotiations and cooperation.

item.title: Kazakhstan Enhances International Cooperation and Diplomatic Engagements
item.description: Kazakhstan is strengthening international ties and dialogue with foreign partners. Deputy Foreign Minister Arman Issetov met with OSCE Special Representative Serge Roomun to discuss Switzerland's 2026 OSCE chairmanship priorities and interreligious dialogue. Ambassador Madiyar Menilbekov met with the new OIC Secretary-General to discuss cooperation within the organization.

item.title: Kazakhstan Launches 13 Criminal Cases After Military Training Fatalities
item.description: Kazakhstan's Defense Ministry is under investigation following a fatal military exercise in the Caspian Sea, which resulted in the deaths of 14 servicemen. Irregularities in planning and lack of oversight were identified. Thirteen criminal cases have been initiated for alleged embezzlement, abuse of power, and other offenses. Five officials have been detained.

item.title: Kazakhstan President Meets Sultan of Oman to Discuss Bilateral Relations
item.description: Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev met with the Sultan of Oman, Haitham bin Tarik, to discuss strengthening bilateral ties. Tokayev highlighted Oman's economic success and constructive role in international affairs. Both leaders expressed confidence in expanding cooperation and are scheduled to sign agreements and attend a business forum.

item.title: Couple Sentenced in Petropavlovsk for Rape of 13-Year-Old Girl
item.description: A court in Petropavlovsk has sentenced a couple for the sexual assault of a 13-year-old girl. The 34-year-old man received a life sentence, while his 32-year-old wife was sentenced to 20 years for aiding the crime. The court banned both from working with minors.

item.title: Kazakh President Welcomes Sultan of Oman at Astana Airport
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev welcomed the Sultan of Oman, Haitham bin Tariq Al Said, upon his arrival at Astana airport for a state visit. Military aircraft escorted the Sultan's plane from the border to the capital.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev Welcomes Sultan of Oman at Astana Airport for State Visit
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev greeted the Sultan of Oman, Haitham bin Tariq Al Said, at Astana airport upon his arrival for a state visit. The leaders held a brief meeting, emphasizing the historical significance of the visit for bilateral relations and partnership potential.

item.title: Imran Khan Supporters March Towards Pakistan's Capital Demanding Release
item.description: Thousands of supporters of former Pakistani Prime Minister Imran Khan have begun marching towards the capital, Islamabad, demanding his release from prison. Authorities have stated they will prevent protesters from entering the capital.

item.title: Teenager Dies After Brawl With Peer in Kazakhstan's Zhambyl Region
item.description: A 15-year-old boy died from injuries sustained during a fight with another minor in the village of Bayzak, Zhambyl Region. The incident occurred on October 3rd. The other minor involved has been detained, and a pre-trial investigation is underway for intentional infliction of grievous bodily harm resulting in death.

item.title: Kazakhstan's National Bank Recommends Saving in Currency of Income and Expenses
item.description: Kazakhstan's National Bank suggests citizens save in the currency they earn and spend. While tenge deposits are generally recommended for those living and spending in Kazakhstan, foreign currency deposits may suit individuals with expenses abroad or those planning large purchases in foreign currency. Banks are now offering higher rates on long-term foreign currency deposits.

item.title: Four East Kazakhstan School Directors Violated Rights of Children with Special Needs
item.description: A prosecutor's inspection in East Kazakhstan revealed violations in the education of children with special needs. Children received 8 hours of education weekly instead of the required 19. Teachers were paid for unconducted lessons. Four school directors faced disciplinary action, and eight teachers returned misappropriated funds.

item.title: Taliban Foreign Minister Calls for Dialogue to Resolve Disputes with Pakistan
item.description: Amir Khan Muttaqi, the Taliban's foreign minister, stated at the Moscow Format meeting that disputes between the Taliban and Pakistan should be resolved through dialogue, not military approaches. He accused Pakistan of using economic transit, migrants, and students as pressure tools and emphasized regional cooperation against terrorism.

item.title: Tajikistan Begins Importing Iranian Oil, Testing New Supply Route and US Sanctions
item.description: Tajikistan has announced it is now importing oil and petroleum products from Iran, opening a new energy source for a country long dominated by Russian supply. The move raises questions about potential secondary US sanctions for countries doing business with Iran, as Washington tightens pressure on Tehran's oil revenues. The US Treasury stated that entities involved in Iran's oil sector face increasing risk.

item.title: Taliban Reportedly Recruiting 1,000 Young People for Border Area Deployment
item.description: Sources in Kandahar province indicate the Taliban have begun recruiting approximately 1,000 new personnel for their military forces. These recruits are intended for deployment to Afghanistan's border areas. The recruitment drive is reportedly underway in Kandahar, Helmand, Uruzgan, and Zabul provinces, with new personnel expected to be deployed after brief military training.

item.title: 13 Criminal Cases Opened Regarding Violations in the Ministry of Defense
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev was briefed on the initial results of the commission investigating the Ministry of Defense. The commission was established following tragic events in the Mangystau region where 14 soldiers died during exercises. The briefing covered the first outcomes of this investigation into alleged violations within the ministry.

item.title: Kostanay Region Drivers Warned of Hazardous Weather Conditions
item.description: Authorities in the Kostanay Region are urging drivers to exercise caution due to adverse weather. The area is experiencing variable conditions, including strong winds, precipitation, snow, hail, and icy roads. Police advise drivers to reduce speed, maintain safe distances, avoid sudden maneuvers, and postpone long trips if possible. Pedestrians are also reminded to be careful.

item.title: Kazakhstan Considers Limiting Social Media Access for Children Under 16
item.description: Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov has responded to parliamentary inquiries regarding restricting social media registration for children under 16. Draft amendments to regulate online platform access for users under sixteen have been prepared and submitted. If adopted, new rules for age verification will be developed.
